media.net interview question
```
Given a list of ‘n’ IP ranges (ipv4), create an efficient data structure to serve queries if a given IP belongs to the set or not quicker. 
for e.g. :
given these ip ranges
[[10.10.1.100, 10.10.2.50], [10.10.2.200, 10.10.4.100], [10.20.200.20, 10.40.10.100]]
To search : 
find(10.20.100.40) ->No
find(10.10.3.100) -> Yes
find(10.10.1.256) -> Yes

ranges can be upto 1e5 and queries can also be upto 1e5, "you need to implement searching in constant time"
```

reported.text: Arrows kill the soldier at distance d_i (badge a_i) and those behind step forward; given all N (d_i, a_i), recover the original line-up (process in reverse with a BIT/order-statistics tree).

sources.passage:
Media.net technical Interview for summer interns 2023
Last year, I got a chance to interview with Media.net for summer intern position.
I was asked this question
**a cannon is continuously firing arrows from the left side. An arrow at timestamp i is defined by 2 parameters (di,ai) (soldier at distance di with badge ai killed by this arrow) Whenever a soldier dies all the soldiers behind moves one step forward to fill the empty space
All the soldiers will die after N arrow
So you have given N arrows (di, ai)
You have to find the original order in which they are standing at the start**
Input:
N = 3
(3,a3)
(1,a2)
(1,a1)
Output -> a2,a1,a3

I couldnt even discuss how will I approach it as there was network and noise issues.
I havent solved it yet in less than O(n^2) time complexity
if anyone can do it, Please comment.

          2. Given a  string  find the sum of all possible expressions by inserting the ‘+’  between the characters of the string any number of times. (Medium: Done by brute force take all  combinations)

  **Round 3**: This was like a Low Level System Design round. The interview lasted about 90 minutes. I was given a doc which had the entire question, It was related to  Inventory Management , 4 functions  were given like Create Product , get Total Inventory, Create Order, Confirm Order. All the 4 functions were to be completed such a way that it works like E-Commerce. I used 2 maps for Listof orders and Cart and solved it. 
There was bonus functionality to be added that was if there is difference between time at Create order and Confirm order is greaterthan 30sec just cancel the order. This was done by Time Module.

**Round 4**: It was Hiring Manager round . The interview started with basic introduction and then discussion about my projects. The interviewer went quite in details of Tech stack of project. Every question was based on my previous response and also in detail discussion like what kind ofauthentication would you use, which kind of DB for this scenario , questions related to JWT tokens (I mistakenly had mentioned this and it really turned out bad for me).

I could not clear this last r

## **Round 1- OA (120 minutes, 3 questions on hackerrank platform)**

1. A prototype to be developed to model a cache in which each entry expires after a designated lifespan. Input is provided as a two-dimensional array **data** with *n* rows and two columns: the first element of each row records the insertion timestamp, and the second specifies how long the entry remains valid. A separate array of *q* query timestamps is then supplied, and for each timestamp the number of entries still active (i.e. whose insertion time plus lifespan exceeds the query time) must be reported.
2. For a given integer k, determine how many positive integers ≤ k have a digit-sum divisible by an integer m. The result may be huge, so give it modulo 10⁹ + 7.
3. Each of ith objects has weight 2^i and a price given by cost[i]. Determine the minimum total cost needed to choose a set of objects whose combined weight is at least minWeight.

## **Round 2- Machine coding (90 minutes) (interviewer will be present)**

Design an **in-memory car-pooling service** that manages ride offers and bookings between drivers and passengers. All coordinates are given as latitude and longitude in floating point numbers. For distance checks you may treat the Earth as a plane and apply the Euclidean formula; a ride is considered “nearby” if the straight-line distance between the driver’s start point and the passenger’s requested start point is **≤ 5 km**.

**Core operations to be performed**

***Add ride***

* Input: rideId(auto generated), startLat, startLng, endLat, endLng, driverName, maxSeatCapacity.
* Effect: registers a new ride with the stated seat capacity. A duplicate rideId must be rejected or ignored to keep the system idempotent.

***Find nearby rides***

* Input: personId(auto generated), personName, startLat, startLng, endLat, endLng.
* Effect: returns every ride whose driver’s start location lies within 5 km of the requester’s start location, sorted by ascending distance.

***Book the nearest ride***

* Input: personName, rideId
* Effect: selects the closest eligible ride (nearest distance, at least one seat free) and records the booking, decrementing the remaining-seat count. If the seat is full, it should show that it is unable to book that ride and will choose the next
